newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, then slips on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, then slips on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended down slightly Wednesday in lackluster trade, then lost more ground in after-hours trade on an unexpectedly large weekly jump in U.S. gas inventories, market sources said.

Earlier, August slipped 1.8 cents to close at $2.098 per million British thermal units, then dipped to $2.085 on ACCESS after the AGA stock report. September settled 0.9 cent lower at $2.117. Other months ended down by 0.5 to one cent.
"The AGAs were at the very high end of estimates, so the market sold off a bit," said one East Coast trader, noting futures slipped earlier despite a firmer physical market.

AGA said Wednesday U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 96 bcf, well above average estimates in the 83-88 bcf range. Overall stocks climbed to 222 bcf, or 15 percent, over year-ago. Eastern storage gained 64 bcf and remained 78 bcf, or 10 percent, above last year, while western inventories continued to lag 1996 levels by seven percent. Producing region stocks, which climbed 21 bcf last week, were still 51 percent over year ago.
Despite some weakness on the report, some expected physical prices to stay resilient in the face of forecasts for warmer Midwest and Northeast weather later this week and next.

Chart traders said August's lower close today negated the possible upside reversal after Tuesday's action. Most agreed the spot month seemed range bound between $2.05 and $2.15. Next resistance was seen along the down trendline at $2.25, while psychological support was pegged at $2.
In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed two cents to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were three cents higher in the low-$2s. New York city gate gas held steady in the high-$2.30s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell 0.9 cent to $2.197. NYMEX said 29,585 contracts traded, down from Tuesday's revised tally of 39,231.

On KCBT, August finished 1.5 cents lower at $1.99, while deferreds ended down by 0.7 to one cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.3 cent to 10.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 100 lots traded, up from Tuesday's total of 72.
